active_paradigms.idea: Model broadcast as a min-cost flow problem and solve with networkx.min_cost_flow, treating each partition as one unit of demand
active_paradigms.description: The current solution routes ALL partitions of every destination along the identical path, which serializes transfers over shared links and ignores throughput. Instead, build a flow network where each edge has capacity derived from its throughput and per-unit cost from its cost attribute. Set demand at each destination equal to num_partitions and supply at src equal to num_partitions * len(dsts). Solve with networkx.min_cost_flow (or nx.network_simplex) to obtain a min-cost feasible flow that naturally spreads partitions across parallel links. Then decompose the flow into per-partition paths for each destination via greedy path extraction on the flow-support subgraph (repeatedly walk from src to dst consuming one unit of flow). Emit each partition's path via append_dst_partition_path. This directly optimizes the true objective: cost under capacity constraints, exploiting multi-network parallelism rather than tree-sharing heuristics.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Total data transfer cost under throughput/capacity constraints, and load balancing across parallel links
active_paradigms.cautions: Edges with cost=None must be excluded or given a huge cost. Flow decomposition must respect per-edge flow counts. If min_cost_flow is infeasible (insufficient capacity), fall back to relaxing capacities or the current Steiner approach. Keep the flow graph as a DiGraph with integer capacities.

active_paradigms.idea: Assign each partition a distinct low-cost path using edge-disjoint / k-shortest path diversity (nx.shortest_simple_paths per partition with marginal congestion cost)
active_paradigms.description: Instead of one shared path, compute for each destination a set of k alternative simple paths using nx.shortest_simple_paths (generator, take first ~20). Then assign the num_partitions paths to destinations/partitions jointly: iterate destinations in increasing shortest-path distance, and for each partition pick the path minimizing (edge cost + congestion penalty proportional to current link utilization / throughput). This is a single greedy assignment loop with an incremental utilization map, not multi-stage optimization. The congestion penalty makes partitions fan out onto different cloud networks when the direct link is saturated, reducing completion time and avoiding paying for over-utilized expensive links. Emit each (dst, partition) with its own chosen path.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Parallelism across partitions and load balancing; reduces effective cost when the evaluator accounts for throughput sharing or transfer time
active_paradigms.cautions: Utilization penalty lambda should scale with cost units (e.g., penalty = alpha * used/throughput * base_cost); tune alpha once, not via scipy. Cap the k-shortest enumeration to avoid timeouts on large graphs. Ensure every partition still gets a valid path even if alternatives are expensive.

active_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing local search over per-destination path choices from a precomputed candidate path pool
active_paradigms.description: Precompute for each destination a candidate pool of ~10 diverse paths (top-k shortest simple paths). Represent a solution as a vector: one chosen path index per destination (all partitions share it, or extend to per-partition). Define the objective exactly as the evaluator's proxy: union-of-edges cost plus a congestion term sum over edges of (load/throughput)^2 to penalize hotspots. Run a lightweight simulated annealing: random single-destination moves to another candidate path, accept per Metropolis criterion, ~2000 iterations with geometric cooling. This escapes the local optima that trap the current greedy marginal-cost heuristic and the fixed Steiner tree. Return the best-found assignment and emit paths as usual.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Global cost of the path assignment; robustness against greedy/Steiner local optima
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep iteration count bounded for the evaluation timeout. Objective evaluation must be O(path length) incremental (update only changed edges). Seed with the current best greedy solution so it never regresses. Use a fixed random seed for reproducibility.
